smoothed_rtt = 7/8 * smoothed_rtt + 1/8 * adjusted_rtt
rttvar_sample = abs(smoothed_rtt - adjusted_rtt)
rttvar = 3/4 * rttvar + 1/4 * rttvar_sample
correct_text:
rttvar_sample = abs(smoothed_rtt - adjusted_rtt)
rttvar = 3/4 * rttvar + 1/4 * rttvar_sample
smoothed_rtt = 7/8 * smoothed_rtt + 1/8 * adjusted_rtt
notes:
Per Appendix A.7 of this RFC and Section 2 of the referred RFC 6298,
rttvar should be computed before updating smoothed_rtt itself.

correct_text:
GetLossTimeAndSpace():
  time = loss_time[Initial]
  space = Initial
  for pn_space in [ Handshake, ApplicationData ]:
    if (loss_time[pn_space] != 0 &&
        (time == 0 || loss_time[pn_space] < time)):
      time = loss_time[pn_space];
      space = pn_space
  return time, space
notes:
loss_time is initialized to zero for every packet-number space, and the
surrounding pseudocode uses zero to mean that no time-threshold loss deadline
is pending. GetLossTimeAndSpace is therefore intended to return the minimum
nonzero deadline, or zero if no deadline exists.

The published comparison allows a later zero entry to replace a real pending
deadline. For example, inputs of Initial=5, Handshake=0, and
ApplicationData=10 return 10 instead of 5; inputs of Initial=5,
Handshake=10, and ApplicationData=0 return zero instead of 5. Callers can then
arm the wrong deadline and packet-number space or incorrectly proceed to PTO
processing.

The correction only prevents the zero sentinel from participating in the
minimum selection. It changes no QUIC wire behavior or recovery design.
Earlier working-group source contained this guard before it was lost during a
later PTO-helper refactor.

orig_text:
kLossReductionFactor:  Scaling factor applied to reduce the
      congestion window when a new loss event is detected.  Section 7
      recommends a value of 0.5.
correct_text:
kLossReductionFactor:  Scaling factor applied to reduce the
      congestion window when a new loss event is detected.  Section 7.3.2
      requires the slow start threshold to be set to half the value of
      the congestion window when loss is detected, which this constant
      implements.
notes:
Section 7.3.2 requires, with a MUST, that a sender set the slow start
threshold to half the value of the congestion window when loss is
detected, and the pseudocode in Section B.6 computes that threshold as
congestion_window * kLossReductionFactor.  Section 7 therefore mandates
the half-window result rather than recommending a value for this
constant; a value other than 0.5 would violate Section 7.3.2.  The
correction states that relationship.

orig_text:
Alternatively, instead of sending an ack-eliciting packet, the sender
MAY mark any packets still in flight as lost.
correct_text:
Alternatively, when there is no new or previously sent data to send,
the sender MAY, instead of sending an ack-eliciting packet as
required above, mark any packets still in flight as lost.
notes:
The section requires (MUST) that a sender send at least one
ack-eliciting probe when the PTO timer expires, but later permits the
sender, "instead of sending an ack-eliciting packet", to mark any
packets still in flight as lost.  A sender exercising that
alternative sends no packet at all, which violates the MUST, and the
alternative is not scoped to any condition.  The correction limits
the alternative to the no-data case already described in the
surrounding text and marks it explicitly as an exception to the probe
requirement.
